Build a small, constrained library of causal HRFs

Source: R/crossrun_hrf.R
hrf_library.Rd

Build a small, constrained library of causal HRFs

Usage

hrf_library(
  tr,
  peak_delays = c(5, 6, 7),
  dispersions = c(0.8, 1, 1.2),
  undershoot_ratios = 6,
  duration = 32,
  preset = c("custom", "standard", "extended", "medusa", "dense")
)

Arguments

tr

Acquisition interval in seconds.

peak_delays

Positive response-delay parameters in seconds.

dispersions

Positive response-dispersion parameters.

undershoot_ratios

Positive response-to-undershoot ratios.

duration

Kernel duration in seconds (at least two acquisition intervals).

preset

Optional preset grid configuration: `"custom"` (default, uses supplied `peak_delays`, `dispersions`, `undershoot_ratios`), `"standard"` (delays 5, 6, 7s; dispersions 0.8, 1, 1.2), `"extended"` (delays 4–8s; dispersions 0.8, 1, 1.25), `"medusa"` (recommended 0.5s medium grid: delays 4–8s by 0.5s; dispersions 0.9, 1.0, 1.1; 27 candidates), or `"dense"` (delays 4–8.5s by 0.5s; dispersions 0.8, 1, 1.2, 1.4).

Value

A unit-sum kernel matrix, with time rows, candidate columns, and a parameters attribute. The canonical candidate (6, 1, 6) is first if present.

Details

Candidates use the SPM difference-of-gammas parameterization with undershoot delay 16 seconds and undershoot dispersion 1. These are candidate shapes, not a universally validated range for every population or protocol.
